12.1: This hymn plays a guessing game. Each verse describes an amazing deed and ends: 'He, O people, is Indra!' Here: the one who, as soon as he was born, became the protector of the gods, so strong that heaven and earth trembled.
12.2: Who made the shaky earth steady, calmed the moving mountains, measured out the wide air and held up the sky? 'He, O people, is Indra!' The rishis imagined Indra as the one who keeps the world in place.
12.3: Who killed the serpent, freed the Seven Rivers, brought the cows out of the cave of Vala and made fire between two stones? 'That is Indra!' Fire from striking stones — just like making sparks with flint!
12.4: Who made the whole world shake, chased away the demons and took the enemy's riches like a winner collecting his prize? 'That is Indra!'
12.5: Some people asked, 'Where is he?' Others even said, 'He doesn't exist!' The poet replies: look at his great works — 'Believe in him, for he, O people, is Indra!' Even the Rigveda talks about people who doubted.
12.6: Indra helps the poor and the weak, the priest and the singer who praises him, and the one who presses Soma. 'He, O people, is Indra!' He cares for the humble, not only the powerful.
12.7: Horses, chariots, villages and cows are all under his care. He gave birth to the Sun and the Dawn and leads the waters. 'That is Indra!'
12.8: When two armies meet, both call to him — the strong and the weak. Even two people standing on the same chariot each call him for help! Everyone turns to Indra in trouble.
12.9: Without his help people cannot win, so they call him in battle. The whole world is like a copy of his greatness; he can shake even things that never move. 'That is Indra!'
12.10: With his weapon, he punishes wrongdoers before they even know it. He does not forgive those who arrogantly attack, and he defeats the Dasyus, the enemies. 'That is Indra!'
12.11: He found the demon Śambara hiding in the mountains for forty years and defeated him; he also killed the serpent. 'That is Indra!'
12.12: With seven reins, like a mighty bull, he set free the Seven great Rivers. He also broke the demon Rauhiṇa who tried to climb up to heaven. 'That is Indra!'
12.13: Even Heaven and Earth bow before him; the mountains tremble at his breath. He drinks Soma and holds the thunderbolt. 'He, O people, is Indra!'
12.14: He kindly helps the one who presses Soma, the one who offers and the one who sings. Prayers and offerings make him stronger. 'That is Indra!'
12.15: The ending speaks to Indra directly: 'You are fierce and true; you give strength to those who worship you. May we, your friends, always speak boldly in the gathering.'
